players.product: NdPr oxide and sintered NdFeB permanent magnets

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ryan Corbett on upstream: MP has hit 13,500 tons of upstream REO production in a quarter before; when Upstream 60K was laid out it was four-plus years and pretty back-loaded in capital, and MP got 60%-70% of the way there with very minimal capital and very quickly; technologies to take it to higher levels, like ore sorting (to upgrade lower grade ore before processing), are being brought to bear in 2027 and 2028 regardless. CFO: access to NdPr is the mining constraint on growing Western magnet production, which presents opportunities including looking at expansion of Mountain Pass. On early exploratory drilling: MP believes it will be able to bring more ore into the blocks of the block model over time ('not going to promise you it'll be this year's S-K 1300, maybe it'll be next year's'), which would extend the mine life at existing throughputs with consistent mineralogy; the existing mining permit stays in place whether the mine gets bigger or smaller.
quarterly_data.figure: 13,500 tons upstream REO in a quarter (prior high); 60%-70% of the way to Upstream 60K; ore sorting in 2027 and 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on the year-end NdPr refining target: asked about the 6,000 tons NdPr run-rate refining production target by year end, the CFO said 'it is still technically 6,075'. MP has been refining at scale for 2 and a half years, versus 7-plus years for peers with similar facilities to achieve the same; reaching the targeted throughput is 'not a technical challenge, it's a mechanical challenge', now focused on materials handling and mechanical reliability (e.g. pumps sized for 350 tons a month get overwhelmed at 400 tons a month and are replaced). CFO: the two levers are uptime and throughput, and MP will not push a quarterly number if it upsets the cost structure.
quarterly_data.figure: year-end NdPr run-rate target 'still technically 6,075'; refining at scale 2 and a half years vs 7-plus years for peers

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on heavy rare earths: engineering of the heavy separation capability started in 2021; cells are being filled and commissioning is in full swing, with the intention of having on-spec dysprosium and terbium product to bring to Independence within this year. Since NdPr refining began MP has been producing and stockpiling SEG+ (samarium, europium, gadolinium and everything heavier); separating Dy and Tb out creates an SEG fraction and a yttrium holmium plus fraction. Samarium separation from the SEG (committed in the Department of Defense partnership) will be ready for production at the beginning of 2028; gadolinium is supplied under the long-term contract with a leading aerospace and defense firm; CFO: the yttrium holmium plus products also have real use cases and are 'starting to be viewed as very strategic commodities' — 'hopefully there'll be more to come there'.
quarterly_data.figure: samarium ready for production at the beginning of 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CFO view on heavy rare earth demand: there is 'a bit of hysteria in the market about heavies'; MP keeps pushing down heavy rare earth requirements per specification through strip-cast alloy microstructure, alloy formulation, grain boundary diffusion and powder particle size (its magnet business effectively started in 2021). CFO: CEO Jim has been quite public that he is not particularly bullish on dysprosium and terbium prices given MP's results; magnet demand growth is one for one with NdPr, if not more, because reducing heavy content moves a magnet from 30% NdPr to 31% NdPr; MP is a lot more bullish on the other heavies. CFO: many OEMs over-specified magnets (e.g. for 150 degrees Celsius exposure the part never sees), so heavy demand 'may be artificially higher' and is being rationalized with customers.
quarterly_data.figure: 30% NdPr to 31% NdPr when heavy content is reduced (CFO)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO view on NdPr supply: the two largest ex-China producers both have minimum price floor guarantees from governments; expanding Mountain Pass and Mount Weld will not come close to the scale of ultimate magnet demand, so either not all announced magnet capacity gets added (making MP's magnet capacity more valuable) or the NdPr must come from elsewhere. CFO: the incentive price to drive NdPr oxide capacity at that scale is 'many multiples of the current price'; sulfuric acid, used by some producers but not MP, has doubled in price since the Iran conflict; 'prices are 110, that's going to take care of it' is 'not even close'. CFO: MP's positioning is 'heads I win, tails you lose' and the earnings power of the Materials segment would be 'incredible'.
quarterly_data.figure: incentive price many multiples of the current NdPr price (CFO view)

quarterly_data.signal: Customer General Motors: CFO said MP was making parts to GM's specification three to four quarters ago; the automotive PPAP (production part approval process) is intense, magnets are now in in-vehicle and in-motor testing whose results take many months, and the process spans multiple part numbers, multiple production facilities and potentially multiple suppliers MP might be supplanting. CFO: deliveries will be feathered into GM's supply chain over the next several quarters, so delivery growth will not simply equal what MP can make; MP is 'very encouraged' with GM interactions and quality and manufacturability so far.
